name: Finnish nationalism
summary: Finnish nationalism grew from the 19th-century Fennoman movement, which raised Finnish from a peasant vernacular to a national language and culture and gave Finns a place among European nations, leading to independence from Russia in 1917. It is a language-and-culture based nationalism that built schools, literature, arts and Finnish-owned institutions, opposed class-struggle internationalism, and in modern form (for example the Finns Party) combines national-conservatism, immigration limits and EU scepticism with support for the welfare state.
scope: Mainstream cultural-linguistic Finnish nationalism from Snellman and the Fennoman movement (Kalevala, Finnish Party, language rescript of 1863), through interwar True Finnishness and independence, with the modern national-conservative strand as represented by the Finns Party programmes. The Greater Finland irredentist strand and the Academic Karelia Society are treated as a minority wing, not the core. Most statements were never addressed by classic Fennomans, so many answers are inferred and low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Finns Party presents the welfare society as something Finnish democracy must preserve, so state-guaranteed care fits modern Finnish nationalism.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Finnish wages are set by collective agreements and the sources show no nationalist line on a statutory minimum.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Snellman's state-building economics (a national currency tied to silver) favoured active public management over pure market allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalists backed state investment in infrastructure and industry, but the sources show no demand for broad nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Finns Party's 2011 programme favoured a more progressive tax system and opposed a flat tax; earlier Fennoman programmes had no tax doctrine.

unions-good.rationale: Nationalism and labour internationalism clashed, yet the nationalist wing of workers accepted unions; adherents are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: The interwar True Finnishness line idealised the property-owning peasant, which implies strong respect for private property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No documented nationalist position; the Finns Party mixes economic nationalism with a business-friendly turn.

cut-welfare.rationale: Finns Party material treats the welfare society as valued, restricting it to citizens rather than dismantling it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nationalist workers rejected class-struggle socialism, and no source shows support for collective worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security-minded but no documented position; inferred as split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Conservative-national Finns Party line favours tough punishment and order, so legalisation is unlikely.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Finns Party has resisted anti-racism appeals and speech restrictions, inferred as a general nationalist stance today.

strong-leader.rationale: Snellman tied national progress to law, education and institutions, not to a leader bypassing them; Finnish nationalism worked through diets and parties.

state-harmful.rationale: Snellman's Hegelian Läran om Staten made the state the central vehicle of national life, so an anarchist rejection is foreign to it.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from rural hunting culture and the Finns Party's order-and-liberty conservatism; no source states it directly.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Finns Party wants more police resources and tougher punishments, and defence is a nationalist priority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Socially conservative modern nationalism; inferred, not directly sourced.

decide-locally.rationale: Fennoman nationalism sought a unified national culture and state, not local fragmentation; the Finns Party stresses national sovereignty.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Finns Party backs tougher punishment but no source addresses prison philosophy; inferred as split.

traditional-family.rationale: The Finns Party opposes same-sex marriage and adoption and promotes Finnish identity and traditional culture.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Finns Party opposes same-sex marriage; classic Fennomans never addressed it.

abortion-legal.rationale: No nationalist doctrine; Finnish opinion across the movement is mixed.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Finns Party claims Western and Christian values but historic Finnish nationalism was culturally Lutheran and largely secular in practice.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the Finns Party's refusal to back affirmative action.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The Finns Party rejects nonbinary gender identities, implying scepticism of constructionism.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Finnish nationalism is defined by cultivating national culture: the Literature Society, Kalevala, folk high schools, national art and architecture.

gradual-change.rationale: Snellman built national identity through education and stayed loyal to the Tsar to protect Finland's autonomy, a gradualist realpolitik.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Finns Party limits humanitarian and family immigration and opposes EU asylum burden-sharing.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: National sovereignty emphasis and Euroscepticism imply opposing greater supranational power.

free-trade.rationale: Finns Party economic nationalism is mixed; no clear sourced line.

nation-first.rationale: The Finns Party states its aim is to defend the interests of Finland and Finnish citizens, who should come first.

open-borders.rationale: Inconsistent with a nation-centred outlook and with Finns Party immigration policy.

limit-growth.rationale: The Finns Party backs peat and domestic energy and opposes green taxes, so growth limits are not accepted.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The party called the Paris Agreement catastrophic for the economy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: National Romantic movement was culturally oriented but not anti-technology; no documented stance.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The Finns Party supports nuclear power and energy self-reliance.

revolution-justified.rationale: Snellman favoured loyalty and gradual reform; independence in 1917 came via political crisis, so some adherents are tolerant, hence only mild.

experts-over-public.rationale: Snellman prized educated Bildung, populist modern strand distrusts experts; split.

central-planning.rationale: Nationalist workers and peasants opposed the socialist wing, and the interwar movement was strongly anti-socialist.

socialized-markets.rationale: Anti-socialist heirs of the movement would not accept public or worker-owned market socialism.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No documented position; the Finns Party supports progressive taxation but is silent on inheritance.

basic-income.rationale: No nationalist position; Finland experimented with it but the movement is indifferent.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism leans protectionist in spirit but the Finns Party does not call for tariffs; Finnish economy is trade-dependent.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Finns Party 2011 programme favoured state investment in infrastructure and industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The True Finnishness ideal was the independent peasant smallholder.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Snellman himself carried out the 1865 markka reform to give Finland a national currency, so abolishing monetary institutions contradicts that tradition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Finns Party defends workers without socialism, but no source supports state-recognised wage-setting bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Fennoman nationalism worked through a Finnish Party competing with Young Finns and Svecomans, and independent Finland was a parliamentary democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Fennomans were loyal to the Tsar as Grand Duke while later nationalists accepted a republic; split.

democracy-best.rationale: Finnish nationalism fed the movements for democracy, unions and women's rights and led to a parliamentary independent state.

direct-votes.rationale: Populist modern strand favours referendums, classic strand did not; split.

workers-councils.rationale: Rejected by the nationalist workers' wing and the anti-socialist interwar movement.

right-to-secede.rationale: Finnish nationalists claimed self-determination for the nation but would not extend a general right to regions within a nation-state.

natural-rulers.rationale: Fennoman nationalism challenged Swedish-speaking elite dominance in the name of the Finnish-speaking majority.

political-violence-never.rationale: Kinship War volunteers and the White side of 1918 used force for nationalist aims, so a never position is not typical.

war-builds-character.rationale: Some interwar nationalists glorified struggle; the mainstream does not.

separate-church-state.rationale: Finland has state-recognised Lutheran and Orthodox churches and the Finns Party invokes Christian values.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Snellman's state was rational and Hegelian, and Finnish nationalism had no scripture-law doctrine.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Hegelian state-centred outlook rejects private provision of core state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Finland is a small state with a defensive posture; the party wants to strengthen defence, not superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Finnish nationalism defined the nation around Finnish-speakers and Finnic kinship, though it also accepted Swedish speakers as Finns.

class-struggle-history.rationale: True Finnishness was strongly anti-socialist after the civil war and nationalists opposed class-struggle internationalism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Finns Party is a workers' party without socialism, favouring fairness but not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No documented support, and the Sámi are a tiny minority within a unitary Finnish nation-state.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Finland had no colonies; nation-first outlook would reject reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Finnic kinship is ethnic-linguistic, not religious or civilisational; no clear stance.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nationalism calls for loyalty to the community rather than self-interest as a moral ideal.

duties-before-rights.rationale: National awakening stressed duty to the nation and patriotic education.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The Kalevala celebrates nature mythologically but nationalists did not develop an intrinsic-value doctrine.

limit-population.rationale: The Finns Party backs incentives for births in place of immigration.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Fennoman nationalism sought modernisation through education and national banks and industry.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Hegelian state-and-people tradition gives no role to algorithms; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Fennoman nationalism was forward-looking nation-building, not restoration of an old order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Snellman's realpolitik loyalty to the Tsar was pragmatic, yet nationalism is itself ideological; split.

direct-action.rationale: National movement worked through language, education, diets and parties.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nationalists sought a modern educated Finnish nation, not primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Nationalists built banks, insurers and publishing houses.

production-for-use.rationale: Rejected by the anti-socialist national tradition.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Nationalist workers' wing rejected the Marxist class analysis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: True Finnishness was strongly anti-socialist after the 1918 civil war.

collective-farming.rationale: True Finnishness idealised the independent peasant.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory rejected by nationalist tradition.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Finns Party supports state investment and welfare funded by taxes.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation as a community with collective claims, such as language rights.

conscription.rationale: Finland's national defence rests on general conscription and the Finns Party strengthens defence.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nationalism ties members to the national community and its state.

state-as-business.rationale: The Hegelian state is an ethical community, not a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Snellman's Bildung stressed education enabling freedom, but material guarantee is not documented.

media-academia-power.rationale: The Finns Party criticises elites but no sourced doctrine.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Finns Party avoids racial theory officially though it has controversy; classic Fennomans were language-based.

organic-representation.rationale: Fennomans and later nationalists worked through parties and parliament.

total-state.rationale: Snellman's strong state was constitutional and educational, not totalitarian.

national-rebirth.rationale: National awakening language was common, but mainstream Finnish nationalism did not speak of decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Greater Finland was a minority irredentist strand and is widely unpopular today.

bound-labor.rationale: Fennomans championed the Finnish-speaking peasantry against elite dominance.

universal-morality.rationale: Hegelian tradition cuts both ways; no documented stance.

single-common-good.rationale: Snellman's Hegelian state aimed at the nation's common ethical life.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred from the principle that each nation deserves its own state.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Kinship Wars and Karelian refugee support show concern for kin outside the borders; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Fennomans raised Finnish from a peasant vernacular to a national and official language.

school-vouchers.rationale: Finnish nationalism stands for public Finnish-language schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Snellman's markka reform prioritised monetary stability.

rule-by-example.rationale: Constitutional state doctrine of Snellman prefers law.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement aimed to establish Finland as a nation on a par with others and led to independence from Russia in 1917.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Hegelian rationalism versus Lutheran culture; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The Finns Party puts Finnish citizens first and conditions welfare for immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Finns Party requires immigrants to support themselves; a workers' party ethos.

class-collaboration.rationale: The nationalist wing of workers and the movement stressed national unity across classes against class-struggle socialism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: National cultural heritage institutions are central to the movement.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers split between class-struggle and nationalist wings, with the latter organising nationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Finnish society gave women the vote early and nationalism did not push legal gender roles.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Fennoman and later nationalism was linguistic-cultural, not racial.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The Finns Party backs domestic peat and energy self-reliance.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The party wants immigrants to learn Finnish and follow Finnish law and proposes language tests for citizenship.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not an official Finns Party position though some members push it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Finland's party-based parliamentary system uses it; no nationalist opposition.

national-mission.rationale: Finnish nationalism sought equal standing, not missionary export.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not accepted by the Finns Party.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist strand says yes; classic Fennoman strand did not.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic ideas existed in interwar Finland but are not part of the nationalist core.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Finns Party supports an active state and welfare.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Race was not the basis of Finnish nationalism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: National movement expanded rights of Finnish-speaking peasants and women.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Rejects colonial framing as a general nationalist stance.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Uniform law for citizens fits national unity.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not documented; Finland protects religious freedom.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Finnish schools teach confessional religion; party emphasises Christian values.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The movement expanded popular participation and national self-rule; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Not a Finnish nationalist doctrine, though Finland accepted Karelian evacuations.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Finnish nationalism treats defensive force as legitimate and sometimes more.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist strand existed in interwar nationalism, but not mainstream.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Fennomans resisted Russification and Swedish-language domination, framing freedom as independence from domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Finland's constitutional system; Young Finns practised constitutional resistance.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Finns Party backs welfare and family incentives, not a population-explains-poverty doctrine.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nationalism fostered a single national language to unite elites and peasants.

party-controls-media.rationale: Contrary to the free press and clubs of the national movement.

party-commands-army.rationale: Contrary to a national army under the state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The party proposes citizenship after five years with language conditions, a middling position.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Nothing in Finnish nationalist programmes limits parliamentary salaries.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Fennoman factions did split over discipline, with Yrjö-Koskinen's strictness alienating older figures.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Finns Party opposes further EU integration and the euro.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Fennomans accepted loyalty to the emperor; modern Finland shares command; split.

church-by-bishops.rationale: No nationalist doctrine on church governance.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalists defend the nation; defeatism is a Marxist line.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: National movement was built through free arts and literature.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Finland's parliamentary and presidential traditions limit tenure and nationalists voice no case for unlimited terms.

recall-officials.rationale: Populist modern strand might favour it while the constitutional tradition does not; split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Finland's non-alignment tradition and later NATO entry make adherents split.

people-in-arms.rationale: Finland has a conscript and reserve system that blends the two ideas.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: National romanticism and True Finnishness idealised the peasant countryside.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Fennoman movement itself was led by educated elites.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Promoting Finnish culture presumes its special value; Finns Party stresses Finnish identity.

death-penalty.rationale: Finland abolished it; no nationalist push to restore found.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic-national conception and Finnish law follow descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Finnish law gives both Finnish and Swedish equal status; the party keeps allowances for Swedish-speaking areas.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Citizens-first sovereignty emphasis implies the same law for all; no specific position found.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Citizens-first economic nationalism and opposition to joint EU debt imply debts should be repaid.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Nationalists saw independence as political and cultural.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: No documented position; Finnish nationalists never framed this issue.

elective-rulers.rationale: Independent Finland chose a republic and elected its head of state; the Fennoman line had no hereditary doctrine.

minority-veto.rationale: Nationalism rests on majority national will, not minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Young Finns practised constitutional resistance against the 1899 Russification measures.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Finnish nationalism ran through diets and parliament towards a parliamentary republic.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: No nationalist line; Finnish cultural consensus accepts animal welfare.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Consistent with Finnish rural life; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Swedish-speaking elites sponsored Finnish education and the movement for the people.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nationalism demands civic engagement and patriotic education.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marxist thesis not held by nationalists.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory not part of the movement.

native-born-offices.rationale: The party prioritises citizens but sources do not address native-born requirements.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist-internal question outside the movement's concerns.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Economic nationalism and energy self-reliance emphasise own resources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Current public interest centres on reclaiming Finnish Karelia lost to the Soviet Union.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not applicable to a nation-state with a Finnish majority.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Interwar True Finnishness was anti-socialist and nationalists reject left-defined founding values.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Finnish national memory stresses the Soviet threat and rejects equating its enemies with the nation.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not a Finnish issue; inferred scholarly consensus.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Preserving national memory and heritage fits the movement.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Finnish army is under civilian state authority.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism and protection of Finnish ownership.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The party supports the welfare society.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Peasant property ideal is private ownership.

single-official-language.rationale: Finnish and Swedish have equal official status since 1922 and the party keeps allowances for Swedish areas.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Economic nationalism favours national ownership of land.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Rejected, like affirmative action, by the Finns Party.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Kinship War volunteers acted irregularly, but state-level insurgent funding is not a doctrine.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The party prefers births to immigration.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty emphasis; Finnish tradition of non-alignment.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream Finnish nationalism rejects conspiracy theories about minorities.

informal-organisation.rationale: Contrary to the institution-building approach of the movement.

religious-nation.rationale: Finnish nation was defined by language, not religion.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Statement presupposes common ownership of production; nationalists keep private ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: True Finnishness was strongly anti-socialist after the civil war.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Nationalists built banks and firms but the movement never took a stance on Marxist historical claims.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language societies promoted purism and proper Finnish through the twentieth century.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not documented, though True Finnishness sought a monolingual Finland.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way rhetoric appears in a workers' party without socialism but no doctrine.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Greater Finland claims rested on historic Karelian ties.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Finnish nationalists have not sought this.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Contrary to the party politics of the movement.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Finland protects religious freedom and no nationalist programme seeks to punish blasphemy.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The party opposes sharia incorporation but adherents split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Snellman's state was a rational ethical community.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The party seeks only a burqa ban.

social-market-economy.rationale: The party backs the welfare society with market economy.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Historic non-alignment; the Finns Party shifted toward NATO after 2022.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nationalists founded a profit-making bank and insurer.

property-franchise.rationale: Finland adopted universal suffrage in 1906 amid the national movement.

racial-franchise.rationale: Fennoman nationalism was language-based and democratic.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mainstream Finnish nationalism sought cultural unity through language, not boycotts of minority businesses.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Finland's own Swedish-Finnish settlement is not consociational.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The party values the welfare society.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Finnish tradition of early women's suffrage.

abolish-ip.rationale: Nationalists founded publishing and cultural industries.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Patriotic youth programmes existed but mainstream is indifferent to drilled uniforms.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The party is a workers' party without socialism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Kalevala is presented as the ancient national epic and the nation's own history.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring war dead is part of Finnish national memory.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Fennoman politics was about language, schools and law, not a cosmic good-versus-evil struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Kin abroad were seen as cultural kin; split on gathering.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement cultivated language, literature and education decades before independence.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Fennoman elites founded Finnish-owned banks, insurers and publishers to build a Finnish economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Pan-Finnic ideas existed but are rejected as unpopular today.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: An internal socialist debate that nationalists, who were opposed to socialism, did not engage.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Finns Party values the welfare society and public provision of local essentials is consistent with it.

person-over-state.rationale: Snellman prioritised the state as an ethical whole, while the modern strand prizes the citizen.

dense-cities.rationale: National romanticism and True Finnishness idealised the rural peasant homeland over dense cities.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Language and culture, not race, defined Finnish nationalism.

racial-pride.rationale: The party promotes healthy national pride, here read broadly to ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mainstream national defence, with Greater Finland a minority exception.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Fennoman nationalism defined the Finnish nation by its language, as Snellman urged.

free-public-college.rationale: Finnish tradition of free education from Snellman's emphasis on Bildung.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The party opposes green tax reform.

arms-reduction.rationale: The party opposed the Ottawa Treaty on mines.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Citizens-first economic nationalism has no programme for restructuring global rules for developing countries.

sacred-nation.rationale: Kalevala as national epic treats national life as meaningful and enduring.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Finland has never had nuclear weapons, so the issue is not in its nationalist programmes.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Fennoman nationalists built banks and a national currency and rejected the Marxist programme.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Greater Finland and the Kinship Wars aimed to unite Finnic kin, though the mainstream today only seeks Finnish Karelia back.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Finland moved to direct presidential election in 1994; nationalist sources show no distinct stance.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Snellman's 1865 reform tied the markka to silver for monetary stability, a stability-first approach; the Finns Party is wary of the ECB.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims on Karelia rested on historic homeland arguments, and Finland ceded land only under war defeat.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Peasant property ideal sits beside national duty; no documented stance.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: An internal Marxist debate; nationalists simply opposed the Soviet Union.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The Finns Party opposes costly climate and green-tax measures.

collective-defense.rationale: Finnish public and party shifted to backing NATO after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Finnish nationalists regard wartime losses of Karelia and Petsamo as forced and unjust.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Finland's Lutheran church is a state-linked folk church and no nationalist stance is documented.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: National unity across classes is a nationalist theme, and Finland's presidents are expected to stand above parties.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: National unity is central, though Finland itself seceded from Russia; inferred as mild.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Finland's Åland autonomy is accepted, but no nationalist doctrine on joining larger states.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contrary to Snellman's rational constitutional state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Finns Party 2011 programme opposed a flat tax in favour of progressivity.

character-from-environment.rationale: Snellman stressed education shaping a nation, but nationalism also asserts inherited national character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Snellman's state was bound by law.

leader-cult.rationale: Finnish nationalism worked through parties and civic institutions, not personality cults.

land-redistribution.rationale: Peasant ideal implies support for smallholders, but nationalists after 1918 defended property rights.

refugee-return.rationale: Karelian evacuees and kin interest imply sympathy for return rights for Finnish refugees, but the Finns Party limits other refugees.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Greater Finland used this reasoning but mainstream today rejects it as unpopular.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Finns Party wants to ban the burqa, the opposite of this.

common-currency.rationale: The Finns Party opposes Finland's eurozone membership and has floated a parallel currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Finnicism is the strand of Heimo kinship but mainstream is cultural only.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Swedish-speaking Finns keep their own schools and institutions in a language-equal state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalism holds ideas, language and culture shape history, against the Marxist line.

no-bailouts.rationale: The Finns Party opposed eurozone bailouts and joint EU debt.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Populist strand says yes; classic constitutional strand says no.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Finns Party opposes quota-style policies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Finland's economy is trade-dependent; no autarkic doctrine.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Fennomans challenged elite privilege on behalf of Finnish-speaking commoners.

history-own-civilization.rationale: After independence schools were restructured to instill nationalism and a state idea in geography and history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Fennomans themselves resisted rule by a foreign power in the name of self-rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Finnish nationalism promoted patriotic youth programmes, nationalist textbooks, and the Finns Party wants healthy national pride taught.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Finns Party sought to end affirmative action.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Pan-Finnic ideas exist but no mainstream imperial memory; Finland was never an empire.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not a nationalist or Finnish welfare line.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Finland had no colonies and rejects exploitative colonialism.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from Finnish nationalism's opposition to class-struggle internationalism and its aim of uniting all Finns around language and culture.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the Finns Party's support for the welfare state and equal-rights tradition; the sources do not discuss female genital mutilation.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Finland's equal-rights tradition within nationalism; the sources do not discuss women's inheritance directly.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the Fennoman and Kalevala project of treating Finnish and its Karelian varieties as one national language; not stated as a rule.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the Finns Party's welfare-state and state-regulation orientation; the sources do not discuss pollution liability.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from Finland's parliamentary, constitutional national tradition, which has no customary chiefs; the sources never address the idea.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; modern adherents are split between conservation and liberty arguments.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the Finns Party's national-conservative tough-on-crime stance; the sources opened do not detail sentencing policy.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: A language-and-culture nationalism centred on Finnish and the modern Finns Party's immigration limits imply expecting settlers to learn the language, though no source states a legal requirement.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Finnish nationalism has no union doctrine; it opposed class-struggle internationalism but the Finns Party's welfare-state stance does not settle compulsory dues, so adherents split.

voter-id.rationale: The sources record no position on voter identification; Finnish elections already use ID at the polls, so nationalists show no push either way.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred only: Finnish nationalism was language-based and the Finns Party sources show no stance on legal precedence between religious interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred: the movement embraced democracy (and Finns Party stresses popular rule), but nothing says whether fair elections alone suffice, so adherents split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed by Fennomans or the Finns Party sources; modern Finland is permissive while the conservative strand leans traditional, so it is split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from Finnish nationalism's liberal-democratic, constitutional setting; no source addresses shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Finns Party defends the existing welfare society (s7) but nothing speaks to replacing it with one cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from Finland's early adoption of women's suffrage in the nationalist-era state (1906); the sources opened do not discuss it directly.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: Finnish nationalism is culturally Lutheran-friendly and conservative, so it would not blame religion for women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Mainstream cultural-linguistic nationalism defined the nation by language, but the Finns Party sources give no view on whether race is a social construct.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Finland has such bodies and the Finns Party is sceptical of gender-equality programmes, but the sources give no clear line.

missingStatements.text: The language of the common people should be raised to equal status with the language of the former ruling elite in government and schools.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1863 Language Rescript and Snellman's campaign to make Finnish an official language beside Swedish defined the Fennoman programme.

missingStatements.text: A nation's folk poetry and oral tradition should be collected and treated as the foundation of its national culture.
missingStatements.rationale: Lönnrot's Kalevala and Karelianism made folk epic the basis of Finnish identity.

missingStatements.text: Education in the national language is the main way to build a nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Snellman named Bildung the most important force in a nation's life and built Finnish identity through Finnish-language schooling.

notes: Classic Fennoman nationalism (language and education) and modern Finns Party national-conservatism overlap in culture but diverge on economics and immigration; the interwar Greater Finland and Lapua wings would answer territorial and force questions far more aggressively.
